name: Sikao Guo, Ph.D.
title: Computational Biophysicist | Molecular Modeling and Simulation
description: Sikao Guo is a computational biophysicist developing molecular modeling methods and production-quality C++/Python software for protein structure, dynamics, and assembly.
summary: Computational biophysicist with a Ph.D. in physics and 6+ years developing molecular modeling methods and production-quality C++/Python software for protein structure, dynamics, and assembly. Experience spans protein conformational sampling, all-atom molecular dynamics with umbrella sampling, and structure-resolved kinetic models of protein binding and self-assembly validated against experiment.

highlights: Extended inverse-kinematics sampling to protein loops, fragments, and intrinsically disordered regions, with released-endpoint SE(3) moves, Ramachandran-informed selection, and clash checks.
Built AttnPacker/OpenMM workflows for side-chain reconstruction, energy minimization, all-atom assessment, and comparative benchmarking of geometric and generative protein samplers.
Designed AutoCLIP, a specification-driven framework that generates PyMOL, VMD, and web interfaces for structural-biology tools; deployed nine tools with testing, CI/CD, and reproducible packaging.
Identified the binding-affinity range that lets the immature HIV lattice remodel enough for Gag–Pol encounters, supporting protease dimerization, while retaining its large-scale structure.

Developed reaction–diffusion models of adaptor-dependent clathrin lattice stability, reproducing experimental kinetics and predicting a critical nucleus of approximately 25 clathrin under cell-like conditions.
Led the C++/MPI parallelization of the NERDSS reaction–diffusion simulator using spatial domain decomposition, reaching approximately 90× speedup on 96 CPUs for a 20,000-particle benchmark.
Co-developed ioNERDSS workflows that turn macromolecular structures into self-assembly simulations, benchmarked on 44,000+ structures and assemblies of 3–720 subunits.
Co-mentored undergraduate and graduate researchers in simulation methods and interpretation of results.

experience.organization: Institute of Physics, Chinese Academy of Sciences
highlights: Developed theoretical and numerical models of dimeric kinesin motors, combining stochastic simulation, all-atom molecular dynamics, and umbrella sampling to reproduce experimental motility measurements and explain how the two motor heads coordinate.
